pages.lesson:
LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 11.3.1 LANGUAGE PATTERNS

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 11
Topic 11.3: Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Language Patterns

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Language Patterns. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: when, where, whose, who and what) sentences, 1. Why do we ask questions?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify interrogatives in a variety of texts for communication clarity
2. use interrogatives in a variety of contexts for effective communication
3. respond to a variety of questions based on interrogatives for effective communication

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

• Today’s maths focus is Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Language Patterns.

• Start with objects you can touch or draw — stones, sticks, bottle tops, or drawings in your book.

• Say the steps aloud as you work so you do not skip a stage.

• Check your answer with a second method or by estimating.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At the market, count 10 mangoes and put them in 2 groups of 5.

Example 2: In class, count the desks in your row and write the number in figures and in words.

Example 3: If you have 7 shillings and receive 5 more, you have 12 shillings.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Solve three short problems about Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Language Patterns using drawings.
2. Explain one solution to a partner in your own words.
3. Make up one new word problem set in your county or school.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five practice questions and solve them in your book.
2. Show your working clearly — not only the final answer.
3. Teach a younger learner one idea from this lesson with bottle tops or drawings.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Learning to Learn: This is enhanced as the learner uses appropriate interrogatives to ask questions.
2. Digital Literacy: The learner interacts with digital devices to watch videos and type sentences. Values:
3. Unity: The learner collaborates with peers to perform task such as watching videos and typing sentences on a digital device.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. when, where, whose, who and what) sentences, 1. Why do we ask questions?
2. Which words do we use to ask questions?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Use objects or drawings when a sum feels hard.
2. Check every answer.
3. Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Language Patterns is used in real Kenyan life — market, school, and home.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
